01 Revision WS - Photosynthesis.docx.a:
Variable X is the distance the torch is placed away from the water plant. / The distance between the plant and the torch.

The further the torch is placed away from the water plant, the lower the light intensity and the lower the rate of photosynthesis. There is less amount of oxygen produced, thus the number of bubbles produced per minute decreased.

The worms respire and give out carbon dioxide, which increases the rate of photosynthesis.

The higher the amount of carbon dioxide present, the higher the rate of photosynthesis. There is more amount of oxygen produced, thus the number of bubbles produced per minute increased.

When the torch is switched off, the water plant cannot photosynthesise in the absence of light. It cannot produce oxygen, which is needed for the worms to respire, so they will die faster.

When the torch is switched off, the water plant would only carry out respiration and compete with the worms for the limited amount of oxygen dissolved in the water.

As light intensity increases, the average size of stomata increases.

From 2 am to 6 am, it is dark and the size of the stomata is small. As light intensity increases from 6 am to 8 am, the size of the stomata increases as well. At high light intensity from 8 am to 6 pm, the size of the stomata remains large. As light intensity decreases from 6 pm to 8 pm, the size of the stomata decreases as well. From 8 pm to 10 pm, the size of the stomata remains small.

When the size of stomata increases, more carbon dioxide can enter the leaves. Thus, the rate of photosynthesis increases as well.

Carbon dioxide is needed for plants to carry out photosynthesis. Thus, when more carbon dioxide is absorbed into the leaves at a higher rate, the plants can carry out photosynthesis faster.

When the size of stomata increases, more water vapour can move out of the stomata. The plant may lose too much water and wilt.

When the size of stomata is large, more water vapour moves out of the stomata and the plant may wilt if its roots cannot absorb enough water from the soil fast enough.

The bananas grow upwards to receive as much sunlight as possible to make food with their chlorophyll.

Observe the diagram that the unripe bananas contain chlorophyll that absorbs light energy for making food.

Experimental set-up: One unripe banana and one (or two) ripe banana.
Control set-up: One unripe banana

Allows us to compare the difference in the time taken for the unripe banana to ripen. This difference is only due to the presence of the ripe banana in the experimental set-up as all other variables are kept the same.

Concept - Gas produced during photosynthesis

Pt 1 - The organism in A receives light, makes food/photosynthesize and produces oxygen.[1]
Partial for pt 1: There is photosynthesis [½]

Pt 2 - The organism in B did not get light, but took in oxygen [1]
OR
The organisms are breathing/carrying out respiration.[1]

Publisher answer: The tiny organisms in the clear container could receive light and thus photosynthesise to give out oxygen. The tiny organisms in the black container could not receive light and thus unable to photosynthesise to give out oxygen.

Concept - Fair test

Different number of organisms / Different types of organism

Alternative answers:
-The lid is lifted to measure the amount of oxygen, so the amount of oxygen is changed
-One container has plants and the other container has animals
- The number/type of organisms are not the same

DO NOT ACCEPT-Lid not closed properly
-Apparatus is not accurate
-Number of organisms

Publisher answer: The number of tiny organisms in each container may not be the same at the start of the experiment. / The containers may contain different amounts of carbon dioxide at the start of the experiment. / The temperature of the containers may not be the same at the start of the experiment. (any one)

Concept: Photosynthesis and experiment process skills

Photosynthesis took place. Oxygen bubbles produced pushed the leaf discs upward

Publisher answer: The process is known as photosynthesis. The oxygen bubble produced during photosynthesis carried the leaf disc up to the surface of liquid Y.

Concept: Methods to Improve Reliability in an experiment

Any 2

Answer 1
Repeat the experiment and take the average (considered as 1 point)
OR
Repeat the experiment and ensure the results are consistent

Partial mark
Repeat the experiment

To use: Repeat the experiment a few more times, check for consistency and calculate the average.

Answer 2
Use more leaf disc in each set-up/all set-ups

Answer 3
Control the constant variables
Conduct in a dark room/same volume of liquid / Use discs from the same leaf / Use same species of leaves / Use identical containers / Same amount of Liquid Y / Same amount of carbon dioxide in Liquid Y / Use transparent containers

Publisher answer: Repeat the experiment two times to check for consistency of results. Use leaf discs from the same leaf for all the experiment so that the number of tiny openings (stomata) on each leaf disc is consistent throughout the experiment.

Concept: Factors that affect Rate of Photosynthesis

Carbon dioxide

Publisher explanation: The greater the amount of carbon dioxide, the higher the rate of photosynthesis. The amount of carbon dioxide in the water was much smaller than in liquid Y. Therefore, the leaf disc produced a smaller amount of oxygen than in liquid Y.

(2) Group A – reptiles have scales and reproduce by laying eggs. Group B – mammals have fur and give birth to live young.
(1) The swollen stems in a cactus plant store water (structural adaptation). Short roots are unable to take in underground water while broad leaves increase the loss of water in hot and dry places.

(4) Air, food and water are needed by living things to survive. The number of flies increased from day 1 to day 17. Although air, food and water are still present from day 17 to day 25, the decrease could be due to disease.

(4) The changed variable was the presence of oxygen. All other variables should remain constant.

(2) Flower Q does not have a stigma to receive pollen grains, so pollination cannot take place. Without pollination, fertilisation cannot occur.
(1) Insecticides kill caterpillars, so more vegetables are collected. Fewer caterpillars grow into fewer adult butterflies (pollinators), so the rate of pollination falls and fewer fruits form.
(1) The shoot is on the upper part of the plant. Food from the seed leaves is transported upwards to the shoot, as is water absorbed by the roots.
(1) During germination the root appears first to take in water for the young plant. Its length increases more than the shoot initially.
(1) Matter has mass and occupies space. Air, a mixture of gases, has mass and occupies space.
(3) Bulb C is on the main electrical path and arranged in series with all the other bulbs.

(3) Oil and water are liquids with a definite volume and cannot be compressed — the plunger cannot be pushed in. Oxygen and carbon dioxide are gases without a definite volume and can be compressed — the plunger can be pushed in slightly.
